content:
Maria Chen: quick heads-up — canary on the new quantized bundle produced a cluster of malformed funcall outputs after enabling continuous batching (~4.8% parse failures). sample tail below.

Ajay Patel: ugh, can you paste the exact output sample?

Maria Chen: here's one of the failed responses (truncated JSON suffix):
```
{"tool":"lookup_price","args":{"symbol":"REDW","date":"2026-03-20"},"meta":{"request_id":"c123"}
...
```

Devon Reilly: that looks like a stream-cut at the token boundary — suffix got chopped mid-byte. Could be kv-prefix + batching interaction or an off-by-one in chunking.

Sam Turner: CI Bot recorded the canary matrix: int4 / raven-lite / continuous-batch ON -> parse_fail 4.8% ; continuous-batch OFF -> parse_fail 0.5% (same Q).

CI Bot: Canary results available: https://ci.internal/canaries/6301234567 (summary in pipeline logs).

Ellie Nguyen: is the baseline mirrored (fp16) showing anything similar?

Maria Chen: mirrored baseline fp16 -> parse_fail 0.3% with same workload. So regression correlates with quant + batching.

Ajay Patel: hypothesize: quantized tokenizer stride + streaming chunker creates non-deterministic tokenization alignment, so stream cuts can fall inside multibyte tokens for certain vocab slots. Could also be small KV-cache prefix extension that increases sequence length and triggers unexpected chunk boundary.

Devon Reilly: quick mitigations we can try:
- add a sentinel terminator token to tool outputs (e.g. "<JSON_END>")
- postprocess JSON-repair (heuristic balancer) before parse attempt
- bump parse retry budget + small jittered backoff
- disable continuous batching for the canary group

Sam Turner: we ran a micro-experiment adding sentinel -> parse_fail drops to 0.9% but changes payload shape (needs router support). JSON-repair alone -> drops to 1.6%. Combined sentinel + repair -> ~0.2%.

Ellie Nguyen: good data. Longer term we probably want to: detect stream-cut in tokenizer, align chunk boundaries to safe token borders, and add a cheap checksum/sentinel for toolcalls as part of the output contract.

Ajay Patel: for immediate triage my proposal:
1) flip off continuous batching for the int4 canary (rollback flag)
2) enable JSON-repair postprocessor in the canary path (opt-in)
3) mirror all requests to fp16 baseline for 24h to collect diffs
4) create a small tokenization test that simulates kv-prefix lengths and streaming cut positions to reproduce locally

Maria Chen: agree. I'll open the canary rollback + postprocess flag PR and schedule the mirror run. also will add two unit tests for token cut fences.

Devon Reilly: add a telemetry tag to failed parses that includes the last 120 tokens and whether kv-prefix was present. we need examples to feed into tokenizer fuzz.

Sam Turner: ping on perf: disabling continuous batching increases p99 by ~8ms for this canary slice but overall cost impact is negligible for the small test cohort.

CI Bot: action items created: CI-9872 (rollback canary batching), CI-9873 (enable json-repair hook), CI-9874 (fp16 mirror for 24h), CI-9875 (token-cut fuzz harness).

Ellie Nguyen: can someone summarize the acceptance criteria for re-enabling continuous batching?

Ajay Patel: acceptance = parse_fail <= 0.5% on weighted workload + no new functional regressions vs fp16 (drift < 0.2 in tool accuracy metrics) across 100k sampled calls. Also need unit tests for token-chunk safety.

Maria Chen: I'll update the canary runbook with those metrics and schedule a re-check tomorrow morning. tagging @Devon for the tokenization harness. :thumbsup:

Devon Reilly: on it — will post a reproducible small script in #eng-ml when ready.

Maria Chen: thanks team. keeping this thread as the triage log — will paste PR links here when available. :rocket:
